short: Spatiotemporal templates on HD-ECoG (M06, M05) reuse the group's gesture decoder; the density claim is untested: standard. Voice-onset and rest anchoring confound the temporal gain.
position: The paper [@ramsey2018decoding] changes the decoder (M06): it departs from the usual trained decoder but is standard, because the same group published the class-mean spatiotemporal template classifier for hand gestures [@branco2017decoding] and a linear SVM equals it (p>0.3, Sec. 3.1). Its sensors (M05) are standard: micro- or HD arrays appear in 5 of 16 earlier intracranial speech decoders (pattern match, Appendix), and the credit to HD grids rests on no density test (Sec. 3.2). Evaluation (M12) is standard for 2017. The strongest confound is timing: each phoneme trial is cut on its own audio-marked voice onset and each rest trial on its midpoint (Sec. 2.3), and the group's gesture paper names systematic onset differences between classes as a source of inflated accuracy [@branco2017decoding]. The temporal gain is significant for five classes but not four in the 1-s window (p=0.046, p=0.064), and for both in the 0.5-s window (Sec. 3.3). The pre-onset result does not separate decoding from feedback, since plosive closure precedes voice onset (inference).
